fish.name: Pennywink
fish.flavor: Gathers wherever coins are thrown and wishes are made. It has counted your change and found it wanting.

fish.name: Gossip Guppy
fish.flavor: Its mouth keeps moving even out of the water. Nobody knows who it's telling, but everyone assumes the worst.

fish.name: Hiccup Loach
fish.flavor: Releases one bubble every forty seconds, without fail. Three villages set their clocks by it and one has gone to war over it.

fish.name: Button Bream
fish.flavor: Every scale is a lost button. Grandmothers along the shore swear the third one down came off a coat they loved.

fish.name: Dandelion Darter
fish.flavor: Trails seed-fluff like a dandelion clock. Local custom says to make a wish and throw it back, in that order.

fish.name: Mossmouth
fish.flavor: Sits so still that moss grows on its lower lip. It considers this a personality.

fish.name: Teaspoon Tench
fish.flavor: Exactly the length of your grandmother's good teaspoon, no matter whose grandmother or which spoon. Scholars have stopped asking.

fish.name: Wobblegill
fish.flavor: Swims slightly sideways and seems embarrassed about it. Pat it gently before release; it needs the encouragement.

fish.name: Thimble Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Nests in dropped thimbles and defends them with the fury of something eight centimetres long. Seamstresses fish here at their own risk.

fish.name: Freckled Fibber
fish.flavor: Count its freckles, look away, count again. The number is never the same and the fish will not explain itself.

fish.name: Naptime Carp
fish.flavor: Has been asleep since early spring and bites purely out of reflex. Hooking one is considered rude, but very effective.

fish.name: Puddlewick
fish.flavor: Carries a small warm light in its tail, like a candle stub that refuses to go out. Nobody lit it and nobody can put it out.

fish.name: Sockthief Minnow
fish.flavor: You know all those single socks? This is why. Its nest has been described as 'cosy' and 'legally yours'.

fish.name: Curdle Perch
fish.flavor: Farmers blame it for souring milk from thirty paces. The perch has never denied it, which everyone agrees is suspicious.

fish.name: Left-Handed Perch
fish.flavor: Every fin is mirrored and it can only turn counterclockwise. Catching one on a Tuesday is lucky; on any other day it's just confusing.

fish.name: Moonpuddle Smelt
fish.flavor: Lives only in puddles that are currently reflecting the moon, which raises questions about where it spends the day. Do not ask it. It gets shy.

fish.name: Borrowed Koi
fish.flavor: Nobody owns it; it simply appears in your pond for a season, then moves to a neighbour's. It always returns cleaner than it left.

fish.name: Fiddlehead Eel
fish.flavor: Spends spring coiled tight as a young fern and unrolls, all at once, on the first warm day of June. The sound is indescribable.

fish.name: Kettle Whistler
fish.flavor: Whistles a rising note as the shallows warm through the morning. On hot days the whole pond sounds like teatime.

fish.name: Inkwell Loach
fish.flavor: Leaves perfect blots of ink on anything it touches. Scholars pay handsomely for its signature; it signs nothing without a lawyer present.

fish.name: Pocketwatch Chub
fish.flavor: It ticks. Nobody winds it. Hold it to your ear and you can hear it running four minutes fast, same as your grandfather's did.

fish.name: Jamjar Sunfish
fish.flavor: Orange as good marmalade and about as easy to keep. Children trap it in jars all summer; it unscrews the lids and leaves politely.

fish.name: Polite Pike
fish.flavor: Apologises before biting. Bites anyway. Manners cost nothing, after all, and neither does your bait apparently.

fish.name: Backwards Trout
fish.flavor: Swims tail-first through the week and remembers next Tuesday clearly. To catch one, cast where it was, not where it will have been.

fish.name: Willowisp Koi
fish.flavor: Drifts under the lily pads glowing like a lantern carried by someone who isn't there. Follow it and you'll end up somewhere important, eventually, probably.

fish.name: Fog Collector
fish.flavor: Its wide gills comb the mist off the pond each dawn and store it, folded, somewhere inside. Lighthouse keepers claim to buy from it. Cash only.

fish.name: The Unblinking Rudd
fish.flavor: Has not blinked since anyone started keeping records, and the records go back a while. Staring contests are inadvisable and, in two counties, illegal.

fish.name: Toadstool Angler
fish.flavor: Its lure is a tiny, perfect red-capped mushroom, which is cheating, and the fairies have filed a complaint. It dangles it anyway.

fish.name: Mirrorbelly Sneak
fish.flavor: Its belly reflects a pond very much like this one, but tidier, with better weather. Some anglers stare into it for hours and come away homesick for nowhere.

fish.name: The Ferryman's Change
fish.flavor: Armored in coins from kingdoms that no longer exist, it surfaces only when someone nearby owes a debt they've forgotten. It always has exact fare.

fish.name: Grandmother Weed
fish.flavor: Older than the parish records, which mention her anyway. The pond rearranges itself around her comfort, and so, you notice, do you.

fish.name: The Pond's Idea of a Pike
fish.flavor: The pond heard about pike once, secondhand, and did its best. The result has too many teeth, all of them proud, none of them in the right place.

fish.name: The Sunken Bell
fish.flavor: A carp that grew around the bell of a drowned chapel until fish and bronze forgot which was which. On still evenings it tolls, and every fish in the pond turns to face the same direction.

fish.name: Duckweed Empress
fish.flavor: Glides beneath the green like a shadow wearing a mantle sewn by generations of devoted snails. Kneeling is optional. It is also, anglers report, involuntary.

fish.name: The First Ripple
fish.flavor: Every ring that has ever spread across every pond began at this fish, and is still spreading. Land it, and for one held heartbeat, all the water in the world goes perfectly still.
